sources.title: Apoptosis: a basic biological phenomenon with wide-ranging implications in tissue kinetics
sources.locator: Abstract and summary: the term apoptosis proposed for a mechanism of controlled cell deletion playing a complementary but opposite role to mitosis in regulating animal cell populations; the two-stage morphology of nuclear and cytoplasmic condensation then breaking into membrane-bound, well-preserved fragments; shedding of apoptotic bodies from epithelial-lined surfaces or uptake by other cells; the active, inherently programmed reading; and involvement in turnover of healthy adult tissues.
sources.license: Displayed as Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 International on the PMC record; facts-only use, with no source expression reused

uses.rightsBasisEvidence: Used only to verify the naming of apoptosis, its stated relation to mitosis in population regulation, the two-stage morphology, the two disposal routes including shedding from epithelial-lined surfaces, the description of the process as active and inherently programmed, and its presence in normal adult tissue turnover. The paper's statement about therapeutically induced tumour regression is deliberately not used, because treatment is outside this course's scope. No wording, figure, micrograph, table or example was copied or adapted; the crypt argument, the two-cell comparison and every teaching task are this lesson's own.

sources.title: Apoptosis: A Review of Programmed Cell Death
sources.locator: Morphology and pathway sections: intact membrane so contents are not released into the interstitium; essentially no inflammatory reaction in apoptosis, against release of contents, chemotactic recruitment and inflammation usually present where membrane integrity is lost; phosphatidylserine on the outer surface as a phagocyte recognition ligand; caspases as initiators and executioners; extrinsic death-receptor and intrinsic mitochondrial routes; energy dependence; completion in 2 to 3 hours.
sources.license: NIH public-access author manuscript under the PMC copyright notice; facts-only use, with no source expression reused

uses.rightsBasisEvidence: Used only to verify membrane integrity and the absence of an inflammatory reaction in apoptosis against the release of contents and the usual presence of inflammation where membrane integrity is lost, the phagocyte recognition role of exposed phosphatidylserine, the functional division of caspases, the two converging activation routes, the energy dependence of the process, and its completion time. The review's comparative table was not reproduced and its numbered caspase assignments are explicitly set aside in the lesson as a lookup rather than material to hold. No wording, figure, table or example was copied or adapted.

sources.title: Molecular mechanisms of cell death: recommendations of the Nomenclature Committee on Cell Death 2018
sources.locator: Introduction and classification: accidental cell death as the instantaneous, catastrophic demise of cells under severe physical, chemical or mechanical insult; regulated cell death as relying on dedicated machinery and so modulable pharmacologically or genetically; programmed cell death as its physiological forms; the aim of defining modalities on genetic, biochemical, pharmacological and functional rather than morphological grounds; necroptosis and pyroptosis among regulated modalities.
sources.license: Creative Commons Attribution-NonCommercial-ShareAlike 4.0 International; facts-only use, with no source expression reused

uses.rightsBasisEvidence: Used only to verify the accidental-versus-regulated distinction and its definitions, the meaning the committee gives programmed cell death, the decision to classify death on non-morphological grounds, and the existence of regulated modalities with a necrotic appearance. The licence on this article is non-commercial and share-alike, which this project does not accept for adaptation, so nothing is adapted: the facts are taken and the expression is this lesson's own. No wording, figure, table, classification diagram or example was copied or adapted.

sources.title: Disruption of epithelial cell-matrix interactions induces apoptosis
sources.locator: Abstract and results: apoptosis induced by disrupting interactions between normal epithelial cells and extracellular matrix in MDCK cells; the naming of anoikis; regulated sensitivity, absent in normal fibroblasts and abrogated in epithelial cells by v-Ha-ras, v-src or phorbol ester; protection by bcl-2 overexpression; and the suggestion that circumvention of anoikis accompanies acquisition of anchorage independence or motility.
sources.license: Displayed on the PMC record as Creative Commons Attribution-Noncommercial-Share Alike 4.0 after six months; facts-only use, with no source expression reused

sources.title: Mechanotransduction and anoikis: death and the homeless cell
sources.locator: Opening and discussion: anoikis given as Greek for homelessness and described as a specialised form of apoptosis following loss of attachment to the native matrix; the statement that inappropriate loss of anoikis is thought to facilitate wandering of cells to remote sites as occurs during metastasis; and the bypassing of epithelial cell anoikis by oncogenic Ras or Src.
sources.license: Taylor and Francis copyright 2008; facts-only use, with no source expression reused

uses.rightsBasisEvidence: Used only to verify the Greek meaning of the term anoikis, its classification as a specialised form of apoptosis following loss of matrix attachment, the hedged statement connecting loss of anoikis to movement of cells to remote sites in metastasis, and the bypassing of epithelial anoikis by oncogenic Ras or Src. The review's own hedge, that the metastasis link is thought rather than shown, is preserved in the lesson prose and in the claim's uncertainty field. sources.title: Epithelial Cell Shedding and Barrier Function: A Matter of Life and Death at the Small Intestinal Villus Tip
sources.locator: Extrusion-zone and barrier sections: the statement that it is not known whether cell death precedes detachment or detachment causes death, the latter being anoikis from loss of anchorage-dependent survival signals; contrary evidence that the apoptotic pathway appears activated before cells reach the extrusion zone; ZO-1 redistribution about 15 minutes before shedding; gaps sealed within 20 minutes; about 1400 enterocytes shed per villus tip per 24 hours.

sources.title: Crowding induces live cell extrusion to maintain homeostatic cell numbers in epithelia
sources.locator: Results and discussion: crowding-induced extrusion of live cells controlling epithelial cell number; caspase-negative extrusions at 80 per cent in colon, 88 per cent in zebrafish epidermis, 67 per cent in cultured monolayers; extrusion reduced by gadolinium and by Piezo1 knockdown; epidermal masses at fin edges and sites of tissue strain with density staying elevated; the proposal that extruded cells die from anoikis; and the suggested tumourigenesis link with the colon polyp comparison.

sources.title: Aging, Cellular Senescence, and Cancer
sources.locator: Definition, SASP and antagonistic-pleiotropy sections: senescence as the essentially irreversible arrest of proliferation on potentially oncogenic stress, senescent cells viable and metabolically active; triggers of telomere shortening, DNA double-strand breaks, oncogene activation, epigenomic perturbation and mitogenic signals; the tumour-suppressive reading of the arrest's permanence; SASP composition; and the late-life ageing role with the SASP able to promote cancer.
sources.license: Annual Reviews copyright 2013, read as an author manuscript under the PMC copyright notice; facts-only use, with no source expression reused

uses.rightsBasisEvidence: Used only to verify the definition of senescence and its essential irreversibility, the continued viability and metabolic activity of senescent cells, the trigger list, oncogene-induced senescence, the tumour-suppressive reading of the response, the composition of the secretory phenotype, and the two-directional account by which the same response contributes to age-related pathology and can promote cancer late in life. The review's own antagonistic-pleiotropy framing is named in the lesson as the framework it comes from. No wording, figure, table or example was copied or adapted; the three-way comparison of apoptosis, senescence and continued division is this lesson's own construction.

sources.title: Unravelling mechanisms of p53-mediated tumour suppression
sources.locator: Abstract and p53-response sections: p53 inactivated in more than half of all sporadic human cancers; p53 as a stress sensor triggering transient arrest, permanent arrest as senescence, and apoptosis under DNA damage, hyperproliferative signals and other stresses; transient G1 arrest allowing genome repair before the cycle continues; the downstream genes and pathways important for tumour suppression stated as unresolved; and the tissue-dependence of whether arrest or apoptosis is vital.
sources.license: Macmillan Publishers Limited copyright 2014, read as an author manuscript under the PMC copyright notice; facts-only use, with no source expression reused

sources.title: Cancer Genome Landscapes
sources.locator: Driver-gene and timing sections: two to eight driver mutations in a typical tumour, often three to six in common adult tumours including colorectal; drivers conferring a selective growth advantage against passengers conferring none; over 99.9 per cent of alterations immaterial to neoplasia; decades to a metastatic cancer; the 90-year-old versus 45-year-old colorectal comparison; APC as the usual colonic gatekeeper with KRAS following; 33 to 66 protein-altering mutations; benign tumour defined.

sources.title: High burden and pervasive positive selection of somatic mutations in normal human skin

sources.title: The Colonic Crypt: Cellular Dynamics and Signaling Pathways in Homeostasis and Cancer
sources.locator: Introduction and sections 2.2 and 4.2: the colon renewing every 3 to 5 days with enterocytes replaced every 4 to 5 days; mature differentiated cells continuing upward until they undergo apoptosis and are replaced; crypt homeostasis requiring a balance of proliferation, differentiation, apoptosis and extrusion; 93 per cent of colorectal cancer carrying an activating WNT-pathway mutation, particularly APC; and the adenoma-to-carcinoma sequence. Senescence is not discussed.

The lesson records that this review does not address senescence and does not name anoikis at the crypt top, which is why those accounts are sourced elsewhere.
